title: Normalized local lattice fibres and exactness on the rational heart
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $X$ a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and finite intermediate fields $E\subset L$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $A_E=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $B_{E,X}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A_E/\varpi_E^n)_X$ and $E_X=B_{E,X}[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. These are the continuous completed coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the derived-complete constructible integral categories with compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], their raw rationalizations $D^b_c(X,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], their bounded localized standard t-structures [prop-weil-localized-tstructure], and the pair category $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], with the finite scalar functors $T_{L/E}$ and associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

Let $\mathscr A_E(X)$ be the heart of this finite-stage t-structure, identified with constructible continuous $E_X$-module sheaves by $J_X$ [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization]. Constructible means lisse of finite rank on each stratum of a finite locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification]. For every geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], there is an $E$-linear functor $\omega_{\bar x,E}:\mathscr A_E(X)\to\operatorname{Vect}_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ with the following normalization. On an affine etale lattice chart of the lisse stratum at $\bar x$, let $(N_n)$ be the normalized finite locally free $A_E/\varpi_E^n$ etale reduction system of the chosen integral lattice [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. Then
$$\omega_{\bar x,E}(F)\cong\bigl(\varprojlim_n(N_n)_{\bar x}\bigr)\otimes_{A_E}E.$$
The inverse limit here is finite free over $A_E$, and an integral map of reduction systems divided by $\varpi_E^a$ induces $\varpi_E^{-a}$ times its inverse-limit fibre map. The fibre functor, these identifications and these maps are independent up to the comparison isomorphisms of the choice of adapted stratification, etale chart, lattice and fractional representative, and are natural in $F$. No global lisse integral lattice is required.

Each $\omega_{\bar x,E}$ is exact for the exact structure inherited from all continuous module sheaves. The family over all geometric points detects zero objects, isomorphisms, zero morphisms, and exactness of short complexes. In particular the fibre sequence of any short exact heart sequence is short exact, and conversely a short complex is short exact if its sequence of finite-dimensional fibres is so at every geometric point.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4),(6), Corollary 6.8.5 and Lemma 6.8.7; etale-local lattices, normalized fibres and representation exactness

proof.text:
Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ for the fixed geometric point $x:s\to X$, and write $F^c=J_X(F)$. The finite-type hypotheses give a Noetherian finite-dimensional $X$, so the continuous rational realization applies. Define, without choosing a stratification or lattice,
$$\omega_{x,E}(F)=\Gamma\bigl(s,E_s\otimes_{x^{-1}E_X}x^{-1}F^c\bigr).$$
The coefficient map is pullback of continuous functions. This is an additive $E$-linear functor to $E$-modules. We will prove that its values are finite-dimensional. The ordinary module inverse images compose: on local pure tensors the comparison is $b\otimes(c\otimes m)\mapsto bc\otimes m$, with inverse $b\otimes m\mapsto b\otimes(1\otimes m)$. Inverse image commutes with tensor products and its composition comparisons, so these mutually inverse balanced maps give the required comparison on sheaves. We use the coefficient and composition comparisons of the continuous realization. In particular, if $x$ factors through a locally closed stratum, its module fibre is the fibre of the restriction to that stratum.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2, Definitions 6.8.3 and 6.8.6, and Proposition 6.8.14(2); intrinsic fibre construction and balanced module comparisons

proof.text: Choose a stratum $S$ containing $x$ on which $F^c$ is lisse. There is an etale covering with lisse integral lattices; refine it to affine charts and choose a geometric lift of $x$ to a chart $T$. Here $S,T,s$ are Noetherian separated schemes with $\ell$ invertible. For a lattice $N$ on $T$, the reduction equivalence gives its normalized etale system $(N_n)$, and commutes with module pullback. At $s$, finite-level pullback has stalk $(N_n)_x$ by the etale inverse-image stalk comparison, and every etale sheaf on $s$ is constant with that stalk. Thus the pulled-back integral lattice is canonically the inverse limit of the constant sheaves with values $(N_n)_x$. Rational realization is localization of this integral lattice. Consequently its rational module pullback is the sheaf associated to the finite-module limit $M_x=\varprojlim_n(N_n)_x$ after inverting $\varpi_E$. The next step identifies $M_x$ as finite free; the corresponding finite free sheaf on $s$ has sections $M_x\otimes_{A_E}E$, since $E_s(s)=E$. Hence the functor of step 1 has precisely the asserted lattice-limit normalization. No assertion that a geometric stalk commutes with arbitrary inverse limits is used.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4),(6), Lemma 6.8.2 and Corollary 5.1.5; pull back the normalized system before taking its inverse limit

proof.text: The modules $M_n=(N_n)_x$ are finite free over $A_E/\varpi_E^n$ and satisfy $M_{n+1}/\varpi_E^n M_{n+1}\cong M_n$. Their ranks are all the rank of $M_1$. The finite-module limit theorem says that $M_x$ is finitely generated over $A_E$ and $M_x/\varpi_E^nM_x\cong M_n$. It is torsion-free: if $\varpi_E m=0$, then in the free $A_E/\varpi_E^{n+1}$-module $M_{n+1}$ the component of $m$ belongs to $\varpi_E^n M_{n+1}$, because in a DVR the elements of $A_E/\varpi_E^{n+1}$ killed by $\varpi_E$ are exactly its multiples of $\varpi_E^n$. Its image in $M_n$ is therefore zero for every $n$, so $m=0$. Every nonzero scalar is a unit times a power of the uniformizer, giving torsion-freeness. A finitely generated torsion-free module over the DVR $A_E$ is finite free. This also proves finite-dimensionality of $\omega_{x,E}(F)$, including rank zero.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1); finite-free consequence of normalized lattice stalks

proof.text: On a common affine etale lattice chart for source and target, full faithfulness of raw rational realization writes a sheaf map as $u/\varpi_E^a$ for an integral map of lattices. Reduction and its inverse equivalence identify $u$ with its compatible maps $u_n$ of normalized systems. Pulling these to $s$ and taking the limit therefore gives $\varpi_E^{-a}\varprojlim_n(u_n)_x$ on the fibre. If $u/\varpi_E^a=v/\varpi_E^b$, the definition of raw localization gives some $c$ with $\varpi_E^c(\varpi_E^b u-\varpi_E^a v)=0$; the same equation holds on the limit maps, and inversion of $\varpi_E$ makes their two fractions equal. Integral naturality gives naturality for all fractional maps. Each lattice calculation identifies with the single functor defined in step 1. Hence the comparison between two choices is the first identification followed by the inverse of the second; on three choices these comparisons compose by cancellation. Different charts compare on their etale fibre product, and different adapted stratifications compare on a common refinement. Exact immersion restriction and the pullback-compatible reduction equivalence give the same identifications there. Thus the comparisons are natural and independent of all choices, without requiring any global lisse integral lattice.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4),(6); functoriality of limits and localization and refinement of Definition 6.8.6

proof.text: Consider a short exact sequence of constructible continuous $E_X$-module sheaves. Choose a common finite stratification on which its three terms are lisse. Restriction to each stratum is exact. On a pro-etale covering of a stratum the quotient is finite free; the free-quotient local-splitting lemma gives a further covering on which the sequence splits. Any additive module inverse-image functor preserves a split sequence: if $p\sigma=1$, applying the functor preserves this equation and the biproduct decomposition. Pull back these covers along the geometric point in that stratum. They cover $s$, and the pulled-back sequence is locally split exact, hence exact as a sequence of sheaves on $s$. Equivalently kernels agree locally by uniqueness, and surjectivity is local lifting of sections. Exactness of $\Gamma(s,-)$ now proves that its sequence of $E$-vector spaces is short exact. The heart is identified by $J_X$ with these constructible sheaves, so this is exactness for the exact structure specified in the statement.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5 and Lemma 6.8.7; local splitting proves exactness of the normalized geometric fibre

proof.text: Suppose all geometric fibres of $F$ vanish. Restrict to a lisse stratum $S$. The etale-local monodromy realization gives an etale cover by connected qcqs topologically Noetherian $T$ and presentations $F^c|_T\cong J_T(V)$. Such $T$ is Noetherian (quasi-compact and etale over the Noetherian $S$) but need not be separated, so choose an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq T$ of the image of the chosen geometric base point $\bar t$; $U$ is affine and etale over the separated finite-type $k$-scheme $S$, hence Noetherian and separated with $\ell$ invertible. Restriction to the site object $U$ commutes with $\nu^*$, inverse limits and localization, and $\ell$ is a unit times a power of $\varpi_E$, so the invariant-lattice normalization of $J_T$ gives $F^c|_U\cong(\varprojlim_n\nu_U^*(\mathcal L(B/\varpi_E^nB)|_U))[1/\varpi_E]$, where the finite locally constant sheaf $\mathcal L(B/\varpi_E^nB)$ has stalk $B/\varpi_E^nB$ at $\bar t$ by the correspondence named in that normalization. At $\bar t$ the calculation of steps 2--3, applied on the separated chart $U$ with the normalized system $(\mathcal L(B/\varpi_E^nB)|_U)_n$, identifies the fibre with the underlying vector space $V$: for an invariant lattice $B$, the finite-level fibres are $B/\varpi_E^nB$, whose limit is $B$, and $B\otimes_{A_E}E=V$. This point, composed with $T\to S\to X$, is one of the geometric points in the hypothesis. Thus $V=0$ and additivity of $J_T$ gives $F^c|_T=0$. Sheaf restriction to a covering jointly reflects isomorphisms, applied to $0\to F^c|_S$, so $F^c|_S=0$. Restriction to every stratum detects injectivity and surjectivity, hence $0\to F^c$ is an isomorphism. Finally $J_X$ is an equivalence, so $F=0$. The empty scheme uses the empty cover and empty stratification and has only the zero module sheaf.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5 proof, Proposition 6.8.4 and Definition 6.8.6; monodromy on local lattice charts and stratified detection

proof.text:
The constructible continuous module sheaves are closed under ambient kernels, cokernels and extensions, and their inclusion is exact. For a morphism $u:F\to G$, exactness of every fibre identifies its kernel and cokernel fibres with the corresponding kernels and cokernels of $\omega(u)$. If all $\omega(u)$ are isomorphisms, both objects have zero fibres; step 6 makes them zero, and $u$ is an isomorphism. If all $\omega(u)$ are zero, apply exactness to $F\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{im}u\hookrightarrow G$. The resulting image fibres are zero; the image is constructible because it is the kernel of $G\to\operatorname{coker}u$. Step 6 gives $\operatorname{im}u=0$, hence $u=0$.

For a short complex $F'\xrightarrow{a}F\xrightarrow{b}F''$ with $ba=0$, the three defects $\ker a$, $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ and $\operatorname{coker}b$ are constructible by the same closure properties. Exactness of the fibre functor identifies their fibres with the three vector-space defects. If every fibre sequence is short exact, all defects vanish by step 6, proving short exactness in the ambient module sheaves and hence in the heart. The forward implication is step 5. This proves all four detection assertions.
